title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck is computing with an algebra map φ on a divided-power (PD) de Rham-type complex. The complex has degree-0 part A^0 = k{X_0, X_1}, a divided-power polynomial algebra, and degree-1 part A^0·dX_0. A distinguished element T = X_0 + X_1 behaves as a constant: dT = 0, φ fixes the T^{(m)}, and φ^1(T^{(i)}) = 0.

The map φ is not degree-preserving: φ(dX_0) = 1 + df sends a 1-form to 'constant 1 plus a 1-form'. So φ should be read as an automorphism of the total (ungraded or filtered) algebra, written by components φ^0, φ^1. This is reminiscent of a contraction or 'evaluate dX at 1' twisted by an element f.

The boxed definition fixes coefficients B_i ∈ A^0 by
- φ(X_0^{(i)}) = (X_0+f)^{(i)} + B_i dX_0,
- φ(dX_0) = 1 + df,
so that f = φ^0(X_0) − X_0 = −(φ^0(X_1) − X_1) and B_i dX_0 = φ^1(X_0^{(i)}).

The NB asks: if X_0 and X_1 swap roles, f changes sign; what happens to the B_i?
1. Expand X_1^{(i)} = (T − X_0)^{(i)} = Σ_j (−1)^j T^{(i−j)} X_0^{(j)}.
2. Since T is constant, φ^1(X_1^{(i)}) = (Σ_j (−1)^j T^{(i−j)} B_j) dX_0.
3. With dX_1 = −dX_0 this equals C_i dX_1, where C_i = Σ_j (−1)^{j+1} T^{(i−j)} B_j.
4. As a consistency check, take the degree-1 part of φ((X_0+X_1)^{(i)}) = φ(T^{(i)}). Use (X_0+X_1)^{(i)} = Σ_{j+k=i} X_0^{(j)} X_1^{(k)}, φ(X_1^{(k)}) = (X_1 − f)^{(k)} + C_k dX_1, and dX_1 = −dX_0.
5. This gives Σ_{j+k=i} [−(X_0+f)^{(j)} C_k + B_j (X_1−f)^{(k)}] = 0.

This is routine bookkeeping. It belongs to the study of PD de Rham complexes and their automorphisms or homotopies (PD Poincaré lemma / Taylor-type formulas) for the 1976 IHÉS talk.

Historical detail: the notes are written on the backs of typescript pages of SGA 7 Exposé IX (Néron models, semistable reduction, Barsotti–Tate groups). That is why the 'neighbouring pages' are unrelated.
errors: No mathematical error detected. All signs check: X_1^{(i)} = Σ(−1)^j T^{(i−j)}X_0^{(j)}; C_i = −Σ(−1)^j T^{(i−j)}B_j; the final identity follows from dX_1 = −dX_0.
Implicit assumptions not stated on the page: φ(T^{(m)}) = T^{(m)} and d(T) = 0, i.e. T is a horizontal constant. These are presumably fixed on the previous handwritten page.
The final identity is not simplified; whether it is automatically satisfied or imposes a constraint on the B_i is left open.
